text:
[LFAC.1.7.2] One rule covers the whole range: **two assertions
with the same key values are the same fact — the later one
supersedes the earlier, its payload replacing the prior.** The
width of the key selects the behaviour:

- key = ∅ (every slot `mutable`) — a **singleton**: one live
  fact, latest payload wins.
- key = one slot — **entity-state**: one live fact per entity.
- key = several slots — a **composite key**.
- key = all slots (every slot `key`, no payload) — a
  **relation**: distinct tuples coexist and identical tuples
  coalesce. This is the key-all case of [LLOG.2.7].

A schema of one slot, marked `key`, is both the second case and the last. They
are one behaviour there: one live fact per key value, which a reassertion
coalesces.

idris.name: Lscp_1_3__lifecycle
idris.note: `Relation` is the clause's key = all slots case (identical tuples coalesce, distinct coexist), `Entity` its key = one slot case (latest payload wins, one live fact per key). The singleton (key = ∅) and composite-key cases are entity-state with a constant or a tupled key and have no separate constructor.

idris.name: lfac_1_7_2__one_live
idris.note: ONE LIVE FACT: two live facts of a singleton kind are one fact, from one live fact per key ([LFAC.1.2.2]).
